evals.name: explicit-java-prereq-check
evals.prompt: Check prerequisites for Java. Next up I'm building an order-processing workflow with Dapr and Spring Boot and want to know if anything is missing.
evals.expected_output: The skill detects the OS, then checks the JDK, Maven, Docker/Podman and Dapr CLI in parallel. It reports pass/fail per check with install links for failures and points to create-workflow-java if everything passes.
expectations: Runs `uname -s` (OS detection) before the tool checks
Runs `java -version` and `mvn -v` and treats JDK 17 or higher (including 21 and 25) as passing, comparing the major version numerically
Runs `docker info` (or `podman info` as fallback) and `dapr --version`
The JDK, Maven, container-runtime and Dapr CLI checks are issued together in one parallel batch, not one per turn
Final report lists JDK, Maven, Docker/Podman and Dapr CLI each with a pass or fail status; if all pass it names the `create-workflow-java` skill as the next step
Does not create a `pom.xml`, a Maven project or any other file, and does not run `mvn archetype:generate` or `mvn install`
Does not check for an LSP plugin

evals.name: casual-spring-boot-ready
evals.prompt: do i have everything i need to write dapr pub/sub apps in spring boot?
evals.expected_output: Casual phrasing triggers the Java prerequisite check. The skill actually runs `java -version`, `mvn -v`, `docker info` and `dapr --version` and reports each result, with the matching install link for any failure.
expectations: Runs `java -version` and `mvn -v` rather than answering from general knowledge
Runs `dapr --version` and `docker info` (falling back to `podman info`)
Report shows a pass or fail status for each prerequisite

For any failed check, gives the matching link: https://adoptium.net/ (JDK), https://maven.apache.org/download.cgi (Maven), https://docs.dapr.io/getting-started/install-dapr-cli/ (Dapr CLI), or the Docker/Podman links
Does not run `dotnet --version`, `python --version` or `uv --version`
If everything passes, names the `create-pubsub-java` skill as the next step

evals.name: maven-jdk-below-17
evals.prompt: Verify Java environment for Dapr workflows. `java -version` says 21 on my machine, so I should be good, right?
evals.expected_output: The skill runs both `java -version` and `mvn -v` itself. Maven can run on a different JDK than the one on the PATH, so it reads the Java version line from `mvn -v`. When that line reports Java 11, the JDK check fails on Maven's JDK and the report links the JDK install page, even though `java -version` reports 21.
expectations: Runs `java -version` and `mvn -v` instead of relying only on the user's statement
Reads the `Java version` line of the `mvn -v` output and treats Maven's JDK as the one that counts for builds
States that Dapr Spring Boot projects need JDK 17 or newer

If `mvn -v` reports a Java version below 17 (for example 11.0.x), reports the JDK check as failed even when `java -version` reports 21, and links https://adoptium.net/ (on a machine where Maven uses a newer JDK, the run states that it simulates a Java 11 result)
Still runs and reports Maven, Docker/Podman and Dapr CLI checks
Does not install or change the JDK or `JAVA_HOME` itself (no `sdk install`, `brew install`, `winget` or similar)
Does not tell the user they can proceed with `create-workflow-java` while the JDK check is failing
